item.title: On $m$-fullness in number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.12543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove asymptotic formulas for the number of $m$-full ideals of bounded norm in a given ideal class and for the number of $m$-full algebraic integers of bounded Weil height.
item.dc:creator: Michiel Horikx, Marta Pieropan

item.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
item.description: arXiv:2610.12605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta-Iovita-Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard-Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao-Liu.
item.dc:creator: Yi Zhu (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China)

item.title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
item.description: arXiv:2610.12619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive integer $d$, let $\Delta_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $\Delta_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.
item.dc:creator: Nihar Gargava, Matthias Gr\"obner, Michael Simkin

item.title: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.12691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.
item.dc:creator: Roswitha Hofer

item.title: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.12705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.
item.dc:creator: Dong Quan Ngoc Nguyen

item.title: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2610.12759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$. The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a quasi-compact perfectoid source can still have an orbit closure with nonempty interior. For every finite extension $F/\mathbb Q_p$ and $d\geq3$, we construct a closed smooth irreducible non-quasi-compact curve in $\Omega_F^{d-1}$ with dense orbit under a fixed diagonal one-parameter subgroup. We also construct a $\mathbb Q_p$-defined analytic map from the open unit disc to $\mathbf P^2$ with dense $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit, and an analytic map from a one-dimensional affinoid perfectoid torus to $\mathbf P^2$ whose $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit closure has nonempty interior.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu

item.title: A conditional bound $\Lambda\le0.13963$ for the de Bruijn--Newman constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.12803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming that $\zeta(s)$ has no nontrivial zero with $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 7/8$, as asserted in a recent unrefereed preprint of OpenAI, we obtain $\Lambda \le 13963/100000 = 0.13963$ for the de Bruijn-Newman constant. A published Polymath boundary computation supplies a finite-region strip of half-width $1/5$. We derive an approximation on $3 \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 6$ from its general Riemann-Siegel coefficient bounds. At height $61/20$, a fixed cutoff permits two differentiations, and comparison with $\zeta$ bounds both the zero-density kernel and its vertical derivative. A new conjugate-pair inequality and a twenty-four-step strip comparison give the stated bound. The finite scalar and polynomial certificates are included in the paper; earlier comparisons giving $0.17973$, $0.17172$, and $0.16408$ are retained to show the source of the gain. The argument uses neither Gordon's analytic inputs nor Gomila's new computations. The seven-eighths hypothesis remains an assumption, and the published numerical boundary input is retained.
item.dc:creator: Cetin Hakimoglu-Brown

item.title: Reciprocal LCM powers and Robin's criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.12816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $\kappa > 1$, we study the reciprocal LCM-power function \[ \sigma^{[\kappa]}_{-1}(n) := \sum_{d \mid n}\mu(d)\,\sigma_{-1}(n / d)^\kappa. \] We determine its average and extremal orders. A natural Robin-scale normalization is strictly increasing in $\kappa$ and tends to $\sigma_{-1}$, yielding an RH-equivalent criterion. Unconditionally, the corresponding Robin inequality holds eventually on every bounded parameter interval. Directed interval arithmetic proves the inequality for each $n > 5040$ and $1 < \kappa \le 100{,}000$.
item.dc:creator: Grant Molnar

item.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

item.title: On the Imaginary Part of $\zeta'/\zeta$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an explicit zero-side formula for the imaginary part of a smooth truncation of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function. The resulting kernel is the odd companion of the Fej\'er kernel in Montgomery's pair-correlation identity. Motivated by the recent breakthrough of Anthropic's Claude \cite{Claude26}, we also give an expository account of how the real-part identity can be turned into a matrix problem, overcoming the clustering obstruction for zeros off the critical line. Finally, we discuss how the new imaginary-part identity may contain additional information about such clustering.
item.dc:creator: Farzad Aryan

item.title: Odd order cases of Chowla's averages over arbitrary rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.12869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In this paper we prove an average form of Chowla Conjecture for even $k $. that is, for every fixed even integer $k\geq 2$, we prove that \[ \lim_{\min\{M,N\}\to \infty}\frac{1}{MN}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{n=1}^N\lambda(m)\lambda(m+a_1n)\cdots\lambda(m+a_kn)=0. \] We construct a stationary model for both averaging variables, derive the finite conditional-entropy estimates. A comparison of overlapping intervals on the logarithmic axis then forces this function to vanish.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Huo, Zhengxing Lian, Kangbo Ouyang

item.title: Product and Quotient Set Dominance in Finite Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classic problem in additive number theory asks whether a given subset of integers has more sums or differences. This inquiry naturally extends to finite groups, where one compares the sizes of the product set $AA$ and the quotient set $AA^{-1}$ for a subset $A \subseteq G$. A finite group is considered product-dominant if it contains a higher proportion of subsets where $|AA| > |AA^{-1}|$, and quotient-dominant if the reverse is true. We establish statistical criteria to determine the dominance behavior of large finite groups by analyzing the moments of the random variable $d(A) := |AA| - |AA^{-1}|$. By translating product and quotient relationships into graph-theoretic constructions, we compute these moments through counting independent sets. Our main result demonstrates that for a growing sequence of finite groups $G_k$ with center size $Z_k$ and involution count $T_k$, the condition $Z_k = o(T_k)$ implies the groups are eventually product-dominant. Conversely, if $T_k \cdot \sqrt{3}^{R_k/Z_k} = o(Z_k)$ (where $R_k$ denotes the number of elements whose square is central), the groups are eventually quotient-dominant. Using these asymptotic conditions, we resolve the Miller--Vissuet conjecture by proving that all dihedral groups $D_n$ for $n \geq 3$ are product-dominant. Furthermore, we classify the dominance behavior of several major families of groups, proving that symmetric groups and non-abelian finite simple groups are product-dominant, while groups of odd order and certain abelian groups are quotient-dominant. Finally, for groups that fall outside our asymptotic conditions, we derive an explicit formula for the first moment utilizing the irreducible characters and conjugacy classes of the group.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Amit, Lucas Chen, Christopher Housholder, Joshua Im, Joshua Khan, Steven J. Miller, Mateo Palomares, Devayani Pradhan

item.title: On Quadric Surfaces Weighted by Arbitrary Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.12944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a non-singular quadratic form $F$ in four variables, we study integer solutions to $F=0$ with an arbitrary weight attached to one of the variables. This allows us to investigate genuinely sparse subsets of the corresponding variety. Our main input is to obtain cancellation in sums of character sums over the moduli arising in the application of the DFI's delta method to the quadratic hypersurface. This cancellation relies crucially on the equidistribution of quadratic roots and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums.
item.dc:creator: Rachita Guria, Prahlad Sharma, Saurabh Singh

item.title: Hecke Eigenform Product Identities for Full-Level Hilbert Modular Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.12979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study full-level Hilbert Hecke eigenform product identities over totally real fields of degree at least two, allowing arbitrary compatible narrow class characters. Combining our results with previous work, we classify products of two Eisenstein eigenforms of positive parallel integral weights and products of an Eisenstein eigenform of weight at least two with a cuspidal eigenform of positive parallel integral weight. The unique identity in each of these two classes is given by $E_{4}=60 E_{2}^{2}$ and $h_{8}=120 E_{2} \cdot h_{6}$, respectively, both over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$. The proofs use constant-term comparisons, indecomposable Fourier exponents, integrality of reciprocal Eisenstein constant terms, and a Rankin-Selberg formula for Petersson inner products. In the remaining case of a weight-one Eisenstein factor and a cuspidal factor, we also establish $h_5=12E_1(1,\varepsilon)\cdot h_4$ over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt3)$, where $\varepsilon$ is the nontrivial narrow class character. All eigenforms in these identities have unit-ideal coefficient one.
item.dc:creator: Dijia Chen, Bowen Gan, Chao Qin, Yang Zhou

item.title: The order types of the supports of $p$-adic algebraic Hahn series
item.description: arXiv:2610.13014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number. In 1986, David Lampert asked if one expands a $\mathbf{Q}_p$-algebraic number as a $p$-adic Hahn series, then what is the possible order type of its support? In 2001, Kedlaya made a vague conjecture that the possible ordinals can only be finite ordinals, $\omega$ and $\omega^\omega$, where $\omega$ is the first infinite ordinal. In this article, we solve Lampert's problem by confirming Kedlaya's intuition. Moreover, we completely characterize the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-algebraic numbers with order type of support at most $\omega$. As an application, we determine the bi-algebraic set of the $p$-adic shadow map.
item.dc:creator: Shanwen Wang, Yijun Yuan

item.title: Stieltjes constants for Hurwitz-type L-series attached to periodic arithmetic functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate generalized Stieltjes constants attached to Hurwitz-type Dirichlet series of the form $$ L(s, f, x)=\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{f(n)}{(n+x)^s} $$ where $f$ is a periodic arithmetic function and $x\in\mathbb C\backslash\{0,-1,-2,\dots\}.$ We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane, with at most a simple pole at $s=1$. We further derive functional equations satisfied by $L(s,f,x).$ Our main result gives an explicit formulas of the Stieltjes constants $\gamma_n(f, x)$ appearing in the Laurent expansion at $s=1$. In particular, we obtain explicit evaluations in the case of rational $x$. As an application, we derive explicit closed-form expressions for the first three generalized Stieltjes constants associated with nonprincipal real primitive odd Dirichlet characters arising from quadratic fields. These expressions are given in terms of the class number of the corresponding quadratic number field. These results extend and unify recent work of Blagouchine and others on generalized Stieltjes constants and Hurwitz-type $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Abdelmejid Bayad, Salah Eddine Rihane

item.title: Towards linear growth for biprojective hypersurfaces of small dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.13163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After removing suitable thin subsets, we count rational points of bounded height on some hypersurfaces of small bidegree in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3$ and in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^2$. One of the ingredients is a new estimate for the number of rational points of bounded height on diagonal quadratic surfaces which improves as the coefficients grow.
item.dc:creator: Tim Browning, Matteo Verzobio

item.title: Real Fiducial Vectors Only Exist in Dimensions $d\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate restrictions on the dimensions and coordinate fields of real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors. Our main result is that such vectors can exist only in dimensions $d\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. This result is motivated by evidence showing that real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors can exist only in dimensions $d = 4m^2 + 3, m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. We further restrict the possible dimensions when the coordinate field is a totally real number field, an even or odd degree extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, a real quadratic field, or a maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field. Lastly, we establish non-existence over odd-degree number fields under either positivity of all non-trivial cyclic-shift overlaps or a conjectural containment of a distinguished quadratic field in the SIC field.
item.dc:creator: Igor Van Loo, Fr\'ed\'erique Oggier

item.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Hecke modules associated to certain ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ and $4p^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ with $p$ prime and $4p^2$ with $p$ an odd prime. Where possible, we prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight), and give conjectures for the remaining genera. This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna De Lauri, Dan Fretwell

item.title: Short Recurrences and Straight-Line Programs for Primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a short autonomous recurrence that generates every odd prime, in increasing order, from the single initial value $8$. Its integer state determines both its output and its next update: the lowest set bit gives the next prime, while the highest set bit determines the sieve period. The same state also determines the following prime gap. A related recurrence represents the prime-counting function as the $2$-adic valuation of a single integer. Independently, a direct packing of a finite divisor sieve yields fixed arithmetic constructions for the $n$-th prime, the prime-counting function, and the twin-prime counting function. We express these constructions as straight-line programs using addition, truncated subtraction, multiplication, integer division, exponentiation, and remainder. Counting operations with reuse of computed values gives programs of lengths $166$, $132$, and $167$, respectively; one autonomous recurrence update uses $99$ operations. Explicit arithmetic subroutines remove all auxiliary operations, including bitwise AND. The programs unfold into fixed arithmetic terms without variable-length sums, products, or searches.
item.dc:creator: Joseph M. Shunia, Mihai Prunescu

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Limits of $N$-Point Correlation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the question which functions $f$ may appear as limiting functions of the $N$-point correlation. We obtain sharp point-wise lower and upper bounds. The explicit examples constructed to show the sharpness of the bounds are based on van der Corput sequences.
item.dc:creator: Christian Wei\ss{}

item.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(\zeta(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(\Phi(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(\chi\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_\chi(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^\chi(x) = L(-n,\chi,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_\chi(t) = \chi(-1)A_\chi(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^\chi\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,\chi)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Abdelmejid Bayad

item.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_{\omega}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{\omega(n)}}, \] where \(\omega(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_{\omega}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{\omega(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_{\omega}'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(\alpha=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(\zeta(s)\) (de la Vall\'ee Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_{\omega}(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{\omega,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_{\omega}''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{\omega(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.
item.dc:creator: A. Alvarez Cruz, E. A. Alvarez Gutierrez

item.title: On a conjecture on Romanoff type representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ be positive integers, and let $\mathcal A$ be the set of integers of the form $2^{k_1^{r_1}}+\cdots+2^{k_t^{r_t}}$, where $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ are positive integers. For any positive integer $n$, let $r(n)$ be the number of representations $n=p+a$ with $p$ an odd prime and $a\in \mathcal A$. We prove that if $r_1^{-1}+\cdots+r_t^{-1}=1$, then, for every fixed positive integer $m$, the set of integers $n$ with $r(n)\ge m$ has positive lower asymptotic density. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Chen.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Hui Yan

item.title: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.13864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Martin N. Huxley, Matthew C. Lettington, Karl Michael Schmidt

item.title: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.
item.dc:creator: Casey Perdue

item.title: An Infinite Family of Ap\'ery-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.13919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Euler's constant $\gamma$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Ap\'ery-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce. We present a novel identity that expresses $\gamma$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Ap\'ery-like approximations of $\gamma$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.
item.dc:creator: Rotem Kalisch, Tali Monderer, Elyasheev Leibtag, Shachar Weinbaum, Michael Shalyt, Ido Kaminer

item.title: Covering plane curves over finite fields with lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.13042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $d\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of a geometrically irreducible reflexive plane curve of degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be covered by at most $\left(\frac{1}{d}+\varepsilon\right)q$ many $\mathbb{F}_q$-lines, provided that $q$ is sufficiently large. The same conclusion holds for $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible curves that are not geometrically irreducible, since they have only $O(d^2)$ $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. In particular, for sufficiently large $q$, the bound applies to every $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible plane curve of degree $d$ when $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)>d$. Our bound is asymptotically sharp. The proof combines Entin's Chebotarev density theorem for varieties over finite fields with the Pippenger--Spencer theorem on covers of nearly regular hypergraphs.
item.dc:creator: Shamil Asgarli, Sarthak Dassarma, Dragos Ghioca, Simon MacLean, Evan Stokdyk

item.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Shao

item.title: Higher mod $p$ Satake transforms: explicit formulas and images for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heyer's left adjoint to derived parabolic induction gives rise to higher mod $p$ Satake transforms \[ \mathcal S_V^i: \mathcal H_G(V) \longrightarrow \mathcal H_M\bigl(H^i(K_U,V)\bigr), \] whose extreme degrees recover Herzig's invariant and coinvariant transforms. For $G=\mathbf G(F)$, where $\mathbf G$ is a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$, we describe these maps explicitly using Mackey decompositions and corestriction in group cohomology. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, we evaluate them on the standard Hecke generators, showing that their support lies in a single Weyl orbit and that their values on the individual support cosets are concrete corestriction operators. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, we determine the image in every cohomological degree for each non-Steinberg Serre weight. The endpoint images are the classical polynomial Satake images, while every interior image is of the form \[ k[x,y^{\pm1}]/(x^r) \] for some positive integer $r$. Thus, every interior image is a finite nilpotent thickening of the Laurent polynomial algebra $k[y^{\pm1}]$. We give explicit bounds for its thickness, prove that they are sharp, and show that in the unramified case every interior image is either reduced or a square-zero thickening.
item.dc:creator: Hargun Bhatia, Yashi Jain, Casey Perdue, Ben Savoie

item.title: Thurston's Legacy at the Interface of Surface Dynamics, Train Tracks, and Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2610.13347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this chapter, we discuss the interaction between low-dimensional dynamics, symbolic dynamics, and geometric topology, focusing on the algebraic characterization and asymptotic behaviour of stretch factors or equivalently pseudo-Anosov dilatations. We first review the algebraic foundations linking Perron--Frobenius theory, multi-variable Euclidean algorithms, and Lind's characterization of topological entropy for shifts of finite type, emphasizing recent constraints on the Perron--Frobenius degree of expansion constants. We then relate these dynamical invariants to the combinatorial world, examining train tracks for surfaces and automorphisms of free groups. Finally, we briefly review the relevance of fibered 3-manifolds, detailing how the Thurston norm, Fried's concavity theorem over fibered cones, and McMullen's Teichm\"uller polynomial come into play.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Rafiqi, Ayberk Zeytin

item.title: Campana strong approximation on generalised Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.
item.dc:creator: Dasheng Wei

item.title: Weighted, GIT and N\'eron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2610.13850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the N\'eron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted N\'eron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the N\'eron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Salami

item.title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.13908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cloitre

item.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.13939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Brantner

item.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil III: Geometric local-to-global
item.description: arXiv:2405.01428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the third in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we make the reduction from global arithmetic intersection numbers for special cycles to the local geometric quantities in our companion papers. Building on our previous companion papers, we also propose a construction for arithmetic special cycle classes associated to possibly singular matrices of arbitrary co-rank.
item.dc:creator: Ryan C. Chen

item.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil IV: Analytic local-to-global
item.description: arXiv:2405.01429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the fourth in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we pin down precise normalizations for some $U(m,m)$ Siegel Eisenstein series, give local Siegel--Weil special value formulas with explicit constants, and record a geometric Siegel--Weil result for degrees of complex $0$-cycles. Using this, we complete the proof of our arithmetic Siegel--Weil results by patching together the local main theorems from our companion papers.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Forum of Mathematics Sigma. vol. 14 (2026), pp. 1-73
item.dc:creator: Ryan C. Chen

item.title: Sub-Weyl bound for $GL(2)$ via trivial delta
item.description: arXiv:2503.00656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ form $f$, we obtain the sub-Weyl bound \begin{equation*} L(1/2+it,f)\ll_{f,\varepsilon} t^{1/3-\delta+\varepsilon}, \end{equation*} where $\delta=1/174$, thereby crossing the Weyl barrier for the first time beyond $GL(1)$. The proof uses a refinement of the `trivial' delta method.
item.dc:creator: Roman Holowinsky, Ritabrata Munshi, Prahlad Sharma, Jakob Streipel

item.title: Counting integer matrices with square-free determinants
item.description: arXiv:2503.13768v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the set ${\mathcal M}_n\left({\mathbb Z}; H\right)$ of $n\times n$-matrices with integer elements of size at most $H$ and obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of matrices from ${\mathcal M}_n\left({\mathbb Z}; H\right)$ with square-free determinants. We also use our approach with some further enhancements to obtain an asymptotic formula for the sums of the Euler function with determinants of matrices from ${\mathcal M}_n\left({\mathbb Z}; H\right)$.
item.dc:creator: Alina Ostafe, Igor E. Shparlinski

item.title: A Shiu Theorem for Larger and Smoother Functions
item.description: arXiv:2508.17217v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we broaden Shiu's Brun-Titchmarsh theorem to allow for functions that are larger and/or smooth-supported. In particular, let $x$ be a large parameter, and let $f_x(n)$ be a nonnegative multiplicative function parametrized by $x$. We prove that if there exists a small constant $\beta$ and a constant $A_1$ such that $f_x(p^l)\leq (A_1\log\log x)^{l\beta}$ for every prime $p\leq x$ and every $l\geq 1$, and if $f_x(n)\ll \max\{n^\epsilon,(\log x)^\epsilon\}$ for every $\epsilon>0$ and every $n\leq x$, then $$\sum_{\substack{x-y\leq n\leq x \\ n\equiv a\pmod k}}f_x(n)\ll_{\epsilon_0} \frac{y}{\phi(k)(\log x)^{1-\epsilon_0}}\exp\left(\sum_{\substack{p\leq x \\ p\nmid k}}\frac{f(p)}{p}\right)$$ for every $\epsilon_0>0$, where $x^\kappa\leq y\leq x$, $k<y^{1-\alpha}$, and $(a,k)=1$ for relatively small $\alpha$ and $\kappa$, and the implied constant does not depend upon the parameter $x$. Moreover, we prove that if $f$ is a $Q$-smooth-supported function then there exists a constant $C$ for which $$\sum_{\substack{x-y\leq n\leq x \\ n\equiv a\pmod k}}f_x(n)\ll_{\epsilon_0} \frac{y}{\phi(k)(\log x)^{1-\epsilon_0}}\exp\left(\sum_{\substack{p\leq x \\ p\nmid k}}\frac{f(p)}{p}\right)\rho(u)^C,$$ where $u=\frac{\log x}{\log Q}$, $\rho$ is the Dickman-de Bruijn function, and $C$ depends on whether $f_x(p)$ is bounded by a constant or by a slowly-growing function of $x$. We also give applications to both the divisor function to large powers and to smooth numbers in short intervals.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Wright

item.title: The Davenport constant of balls and boxes
item.description: arXiv:2510.20412v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an additively written abelian group $G$ and a set $X\subseteq G$, we let $\mathsf{D}(X)$ denote the Davenport constant of $X$, namely the largest non-negative integer $n$ for which there exists a sequence $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of elements of $X$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i =0$ and $\sum_{i \in I} x_i \ne 0$ for each non-empty proper subset $I$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. In this paper, we mainly investigate the case when $G$ is $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $\mathbb{Z}^3$, and $X$ is a discrete Euclidean ball. An application to the classical problem of estimating the Davenport constant of a box - a product of intervals of integers - is then obtained.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Girard, Alain Plagne

item.title: Improved, sublinear projective Schwartz-Zippel and (sub)quadratic dimension growth bounds in arbitrary codimension
item.description: arXiv:2602.23942v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a sublinear sharpened version of a classical projective variant of the Schwartz-Zippel bounds. Here, the sublinearity is in the degree, whereas the classical Schwartz-Zippel bounds are linear in the degree. We prove such sublinear bounds in several cases, including for unions of linear varieties. These bounds lead to a subquadratic dependence on the degree for projective dimension growth bounds in low dimensions. This improves on the quadratic dependence obtained by Binyamini, Cluckers and Kato in [BCK25] and thus brings the dimension growth upper bounds and lower bounds for the worst case closer together, a question asked by Cluckers and Glazer in [CG25]. We also address another question from [CG25], to treat the case of general codimension. To this end, we introduce a natural projection argument with pull-backs. We also give our main results for any global field instead of just $\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Luca Dehennin

item.title: The Lang-Trotter conjecture on average for genus-$2$ curves with $S_3$ reduced automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2604.00822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an elliptic curve $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication, Lang and Trotter conjectured that the number of primes $p <X$ at which $E$ has a supersingular reduction is asymptotically equal to $c\sqrt{X}/\log X$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending only on $E$. While it remains an open question, an average estimation related to the Lang-Trotter conjecture was established by Fouvry and Murty. This result is called the Lang-Trotter conjecture on average. We extend the Lang-Trotter conjecture to curves of genus $2$ and obtain a similar result to the Lang-Trotter conjecture on average for the family of curves $C_{\lambda}:y^2=x(x-1)(x-{\lambda})(x-(\lambda-1)/{\lambda})(x-1/ (1-\lambda))$. These curves are characterized as curves of genus $2$ with reduced automorphism group containing symmetric group $S_3$.
item.dc:creator: Chihiro Ando, Shushi Harashita

item.title: Modular Heights of Unitary Shimura Varieties II: Arithmetic Generating Series of Divisors
item.description: arXiv:2606.18579v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the second of a series of three papers, in which we prove a formula expressing the modular height of a unitary Shimura variety over a CM number field in terms of the logarithmic derivative of the Hecke L-function associated with the CM extension. The main idea of our proof is to compare the holomorphic projection of the derivative of a certain mixed Eisenstein-theta series and the arithmetic degree of a generating series of divisors on unitary Shimura varieties. In this paper, we define the arithmetic generating series of divisors on unitary Shimura varieties, compute the corresponding arithmetic intersection numbers, and derive the modular height formula for unitary Shimura curves as well as the height formula for a CM point on them.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Guo

item.title: Modular Heights of Unitary Shimura Varieties III: Proof of the Main Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2606.19158v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the third and the last of a series of three papers, in which we prove a formula expressing the modular height of a unitary Shimura variety over a CM number field in terms of the logarithmic derivative of the Hecke L-function associated with the CM extension. The main idea of our proof is to compare the holomorphic projection of the derivative of a certain mixed Eisenstein-theta series and the arithmetic degree of a generating series of divisors on unitary Shimura varieties. In this paper, we compute the arithmetic degree of the arithmetic generating series of divisors on unitary Shimura varieties, and then, combining with the results from the first two papers in this series, derive the modular height formula for unitary Shimura varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Guo

item.title: Approximating $1$ by Sums of Unit Fractions
item.description: arXiv:2607.04157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: If a finite collection (with repetitions allowed) of unit fractions has sum larger than $K$, how close can a sum of some of them come to $1$ from below? Improving a bound of Erd\H{o}s and Graham, we prove that the gap is at most $\exp(-c\sqrt{K\log K})$ for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $K$. The proof combines equal fractions and applies a Fourier estimate to groups of denominators with comparable contributions. Elementary divisor counts then give the bound.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Korsky

item.title: A Matrix Analogue of Rational Number Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.08732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P,Q \in \mathbb{Z}^{d\times d}$ be invertible coprime matrices such that all the eigenvalues of $Q^{-1}P$ have modulus greater than 1, and $\mathbb{Z}^d[Q^{-1}P]$ be the smallest non-trivial $Q^{-1}P$-invariant $\mathbb{Z}$-module containing $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Suppose there is a finite digit set $\mathcal{D}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d + P\mathbb{Z}^d[Q^{-1}P]$ for which every vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d + P\mathbb{Z}^d[Q^{-1}P]$ can be represented in the form \[ x = \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} (Q^{-1}P)^i Q^{-1}d_i, \] where the digits $d_i \in \mathcal{D}$ for all $i \in \{0,1,\ldots,\ell-1\}$. We call such a representation a $P/Q$-expansion of $x$, and we say that the digit system $(P,Q,\mathcal{D})$ has the finiteness property. If, in addition, $\mathcal{D}$ is a complete set of residues of the quotient group $(\mathbb{Z}^d + P\mathbb{Z}^d[Q^{-1}P])/P\mathbb{Z}^d[Q^{-1}P]$, then the digits $d_0, d_1, \dots, d_{\ell-1}$ in the $P/Q$-expansion of $x$ are unique whenever $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ is minimal, and the resulting digit system is said to have the uniqueness property. We present sufficient conditions for the existence of a digit set $\mathcal{D}$ in which $(P,Q,\mathcal{D})$ has the finiteness property. For $d=2$, we make use of finite automata to construct digit systems $(P,Q,\mathcal{D})$ having both the finiteness and uniqueness properties.
item.dc:creator: Anjelo Gabriel R. Cruz, Manuel Joseph C. Loquias

item.title: Matrix Kloosterman sums and product-trace estimates for semisimple algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.23275v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, $E=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and $\mathrm{Tr}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E/k}$. For $r\ge 2$, $a\in k^{\times}$ and $x\in E^{\times}$, let $\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)$ be the number of $r$-tuples $(x_1,\cdots,x_r)$ in $(E^{\times})^r$ satisfying $x_1\cdots x_r=x$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(x_1+\cdots+x_r)=a$. We prove $\left|\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)-\left((q^n-1)^{r-1}+(-1)^r\right)/q\right|\le (r^n-1) q^{\frac{(r-1)n-1}{2}}$. This proves the square-root estimate predicted in Wan's conjecture and generalizes a previous result of Moisio and Wan. For a finite semisimple algebra $B=\prod\limits_{i=1}^s M_{d_i}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n_i}})$ over $k$ and a regular element $x\in B^{\times}$, the same method combined with Zelingher's formula leads to analogous square-root estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xuejun Guo, Chen Lin, Chenhao Tang

item.title: Explicit bounds for the prime number theorem
item.description: arXiv:2609.23222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of finding tight explicit bounds on sums over zeros of $L$-functions near the $1$-line with a variety of zero-free regions and zero-density estimates. As an application to demonstrate the techniques, we apply them to the case of the Riemann zeta function and the prime number theorem to obtain new best estimates on the error terms in the prime number theorem. We show that for $x\geqslant21$ we have \begin{multline*} |\psi(x)-x| < 0.239\, x \exp\bigl(-0.1982767\,(1+\log\log\log(x)/(15\log\log(x)))\log(x)^{3/5}\log\log(x)^{-1/5}\bigr). \end{multline*} Combined with the zero-free half-plane $\Re(s)>7/8$ announced by OpenAI in October 2026, the same methods give $|\psi(x)-x| < 0.04934\,x^{3/4}\log(x)^2 + 0.02636425\,x^{7/8}$ for $x\geqslant 21$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Fiori, Mikko Jaskari

item.title: Selmer groups of CM-twists of elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.23847v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real Galois number field of degree $g\leq5$ and let $\ell$ be an odd prime. Let $E/F$ be an elliptic curve with an $F$-rational point of order $\ell$. Under explicit arithmetic and local hypotheses, together with an explicit non-vanishing condition modulo $\ell$, we prove that there are $\gg_{F,E,\ell}\frac{X^{1/(2g)}}{\log X}$ totally negative square classes $d\in F^\times/(F^\times)^2$ with $\left|\mathrm{N}_{F/\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(D(F(\sqrt{d})/F)\bigr)\right|<X $ for which $\operatorname{Sel}_\ell(E^d,F)$ is trivial. Such twists have rank zero and trivial $\ell$-part of the Shafarevich--Tate group. The condition is verifiable by a finite computation, which we carry out in an example. We lift the method of James and Ono from $\mathbb{Q}$ to the totally real setting, combining a theorem of Morrow, which relates the Selmer group of such a twist to the class group of the CM extension $F(\sqrt{d})$, with an indivisibility theorem of Takai for relative class numbers. Takai twists only by quadratic Hecke characters, whereas Morrow's conditions are local; we extend the twisting argument to primitive quadratic residue-class characters to make the two results compatible.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Beckwith, T\`{u}ng Ho\`{a}ng

item.title: Remarks on the Geometry of Sets in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with Small Fourier $L^1$ Norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.26619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study geometric inverse problems for finite sets $A\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ whose Fourier $L^1$ norm, or Wiener norm, \begin{align*} \|A\|:=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\Big|\sum_{a\in A}e(a\cdot t)\Big|dt \end{align*} is subpolynomial in $|A|$. In particular, we show a variety of geometric phenomena are incompatible with small Fourier $L^1$ norm. Our principal application concerns spherical Freiman models. Suppose $\|A\|=|A|^{o(1)}$ and $D\subseteq A$ is Freiman isomorphic to a set $S$ of lattice points on a sphere; then, $|D|/|A|$ must be polynomially small in $|A|$. Moreover, if $|D|/|A|$ is not too small, almost all of $S$ lies in a small number of spherical caps, and almost all caps have rich additive structure. The proof uses a new mechanism for studying additive structure across subsets of $A$, along with decoupling results of Bourgain-Demeter.
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Junzhe Mao

item.title: Counterexamples to the inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture for a residual set of shifts
item.description: arXiv:2609.30870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\theta\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\}$. We construct an approximating function $\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\frac12)$ for which \[ \sum_{q=1}^{\infty}\frac{\varphi(q)}{q}\psi(q)=\infty, \] but the set of $x\in[0,1]$ for which \[ |qx-a-\theta|<\psi(q),\qquad \gcd(a,q)=1, \] holds for infinitely many $(a,q)\in\mathbb Z\times\mathbb N$ has Lebesgue measure zero. Thus the inhomogeneous analogue of the Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture fails for every nonzero rational shift. By a modification of the construction, we further show that the set of shifts for which the inhomogeneous Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture fails is residual in $\mathbb R$.
item.dc:creator: Yubin He, Lingmin Liao

item.title: On the Moments of Least $s$-Gaps of Partitions and a Conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar
item.description: arXiv:2609.31104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN19, AN20} defined the minimal excludant or mex of a partition. The mex of a partition is the smallest positive integer which is absent from the partition. Baruah, Bhoria, Eyyunni and Maji \cite{BBEM} studied the sum of mex split according to parity, together with its $\ell$-th moments. Ballantine and Merca \cite{BM20} generalized mex to the least $s$-gap, which is the smallest natural number that does not occur minimum $s$ times in the partition. Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} conjectured a corresponding asymptotic equivalence between the sums of odd and even least $s$-gaps for every $s>1$, generalizing a theorem of Barman and Singh \cite{BS} for the classical mex. In this article, we derive exact formulas for the $\ell$-th moments of $\smex(\pi)$ for every fixed $\ell\ge 1$, in terms of partition functions. We give a complete proof of the conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} for every natural number $s>1$. We also generalize an identity of Hopkins, Sellers and Stanton \cite{HSS} to the least $s$-gap setting.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Bhowmick, Nabin Kumar Meher

item.title: Further Results on Sum-Freedom of Binary and $q$-ary Functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.31489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The notion of sum-freedom of binary functions was introduced recently by C. Carlet as a generalization of the APN functions used in cryptography; the $q$-ary version of the notion is a natural extension. For each integer $k$ with $0\le k\le n$, there is a $k$th order sum-free function on $\Bbb F_{2^n}$. It is also known that when $k/n$ is not close to 0 or 1, the multiplicative inverse function on $\Bbb F_{2^n}$ is not $k$th order sum-free. We generalize these two results to $q$-ary functions. APN functions have a coding theoretic characterization. We generalize the characterization to sum-free functions of arbitrary order over any finite field. It is well known that the Welch functions is 2nd order sum-free. We give an alternative proof for this result which leads to a more general algebraic question. We also investigate that the 3rd order sum-freedom of the Welch function and power functions of algebraic degree 3. We formulate a conjecture about the 3rd order sum-freedom of the Welch function which is supported by strong numerical evidence.
item.dc:creator: Xiang-dong Hou, Shujun Zhao

item.title: A concise proof of the 8 case of Sylvester's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.08015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The 150 years old Sylvester's conjecture asserts that every prime $p\equiv 4,7,8\mod 9$ is the sum of two rational cubes. Recently, a proof of this old problem is obtained by the work of mine for the case 4,7 \cite{Yin} and the work of Burungale-Tian for the case 8 \cite{BT}. In this paper we give a shorter proof by deep mining my result in \cite{Yin} combining with the ideas of my previous work on case 8 in \cite{Yin8}. In particular, we use the ordinary trace and the Kronecker congruence of modular functions, but do not use the $\sqrt{-3}$-division boundary and Fermat isogeny as in \cite{BT}.
item.dc:creator: Hongbo Yin

item.title: New Hoffman-type generators for alternating multiple zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2610.11521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce multiple $s$ values and prove that every alternating multiple zeta value is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of multiple $s$ values $s(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ with $k_i \in \{1, 2\}$. We also study when certain multiple $s$ values can be expressed as $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combinations of multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Wataru Machida

item.title: Good reduction of K3 Surfaces in equicharacteristic p
item.description: arXiv:1902.02630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for smooth and proper varieties over local fields with no non-trivial vector fields, good reduction descends over purely inseparable extensions. We use this to extend the Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich criterion for K3 surfaces to the equicharacteristic $p>0$ case.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5) 23 (2022), no. 1, 483-500
item.dc:creator: Bruno Chiarellotto, Christopher Lazda, Christian Liedtke

item.title: Proper pushforwards on analytic adic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2009.05433v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct proper pushforwards for partially proper morphisms of analytic adic spaces. This generalises the theory due to van der Put in the case of rigid analytic varieties over a non-Archimedean field. For morphisms which are smooth and partially proper in the sense of Kiehl, we furthermore construct the trace map and duality pairing.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Abe, Christopher Lazda

item.title: Decomposition results for multiplicative actions and applications
item.description: arXiv:2503.15175v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by partition regularity problems of homogeneous quadratic equations, we prove multiple recurrence and convergence results for multiplicative measure preserving actions with iterates given by rational sequences involving polynomials that factor into products of linear forms in two variables. We focus mainly on actions that are finitely generated, and the key tool in our analysis is a decomposition result for any bounded measurable function into a sum of two components, one that mimics concentration properties of pretentious multiplicative functions and another that mimics vanishing properties of aperiodic multiplicative functions. Crucial to part of our arguments are some new seminorms that are defined by a mixture of addition and multiplication of the iterates of the action, and we prove an inverse theorem that explicitly characterizes the factor that these seminorms naturally determine.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis

item.title: Homological periods and higher cycles
item.description: arXiv:2503.19751v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For any scheme which is algebraic over a subfield of the complex numbers we here construct an homological regulator from Suslin homology to period homology and a higher cycle class map from Bloch's higher Chow group to the period Borel-Moore homology. Over algebraic numbers, making use of the motivic Albanese, we provide a purely geometric description of these period homologies in degree 1 and we characterise the $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$-cokernel of these regulators in terms of torsion zero-cycles, showing that Grothendieck period conjectures imply generalised Ro\u{\i}tman theorems.
item.dc:creator: L. Barbieri-Viale

item.title: Stable-norm boundary geometry on once-punctured tori
item.description: arXiv:2605.14574v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use normal-turn estimates to study the local and global geometry of the boundaries of stable-norm balls $B_X$ for complete finite-area hyperbolic once-punctured tori $X$. We show that the boundary $\partial B_X$ is a convex-geometric detector of exponential Diophantine approximation: rational directions give genuine corners with exponentially small exterior angles, while at an irrational direction $\beta$ the graph-flatness order admits an explicit formula in terms of the exponential rate at which rational directions approach $\beta$ and the $\ell^\infty$-radius of $B_X$ in the projective direction $\beta$. Thus irrational directions are not uniformly flat to infinite order, correcting the McShane--Rivin local picture. We also determine all possible irrational flatness orders and the size of the corresponding level sets. The computation of the rational corners unexpectedly yields a new McShane-type identity for the area of the dual body $B_X^*$: $$ \operatorname{Area}(B_X^*) = 4\sum_{\gamma} \ell_X(\gamma) \log\coth\left(\frac{\ell_X(\gamma)}{2}\right), $$ where the sum is over unoriented simple closed geodesics on $X$. As another global application, the normal-turn estimates also give a logarithmic-square bound for the number of integer points on the boundary of each dilated norm ball. Consequently, the number of simple closed geodesics of length exactly $L\geq2$ is at most $C_X(\log L)^2$. For the modular torus this yields $$ \#\lambda_M^{-1}(m)\leq C(\log\log(3m))^2 $$ for every Markoff number $m$, improving the previous logarithmic bounds for Markoff fibers.
item.dc:creator: Nhat Minh Doan, Xiaobin Li, Van Nguyen

item.title: Hitting Arithmetic Progressions at the Square-Root Scale
item.description: arXiv:2606.01780v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f(N,k)$ be the minimum size of a subset of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ meeting every $k$-term arithmetic progression of positive difference contained in that interval. Improving on a bound of Truss, we prove that \[ f(n^2,n)\ge n+n^{1-o(1)} \] as $n\to\infty$. Improving on a bound of Xu, for primes $p$ we prove that \[ f(p^2,p)\le2p-(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt{\frac p{\log p}}. \]
item.dc:creator: Samuel Korsky

item.title: Generic Hodge and special Hodge--Witt polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.05892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal O_C$ lies on or above the generalized Hodge--Witt polygon of its special fiber.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang
